intro.title: Rainwater harvesting: size your tank and autonomy
intro.body: WaterPulse is a free rainwater harvesting calculator. Enter your location, roof area and uses (toilet, laundry, garden) to estimate collectable water, yearly needs and a recommended tank volume for about 21 days of reserve.

how.title: How to size a rainwater tank?
how.lead: In a few steps, get a clear estimate for your water autonomy project.

steps.title: 1. Locate your roof
steps.body: Pick a country and city, or use the map and GPS. WaterPulse fetches average yearly rainfall (mm) via Open-Meteo.

steps.title: 2. Describe roof and uses
steps.body: Enter roof area in m², roof type (tiles, flat, metal), household size and target uses: garden, toilet, laundry.

steps.title: 3. Review tank and autonomy
steps.body: The calculator shows collectable water, needs, recommended tank volume and an indicative autonomy percentage.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.lead: Short answers to get the most from this rainwater calculator.

items.question: How is collectable water calculated?
items.answer: Collectable water (L/year) = roof area (m²) × rainfall (mm) × roof coefficient × 0.9 (filtration). One millimetre on 1 m² equals 1 litre.

items.question: How is tank volume chosen?
items.answer: The recommended volume is about 21 days of reserve based on the minimum of collectable water and yearly needs, then rounded to a common tank size.

items.question: Where does rainfall data come from?
items.answer: Averages are derived from the Open-Meteo Archive API (multi-year history) for your latitude and longitude.

items.question: Do results replace a professional study?
items.answer: No. WaterPulse provides an indicative estimate. A site survey remains necessary for a final design.

privacy.title: Privacy policy

sections.heading: 1. Who we are
paragraphs: WaterPulse (https://waterpulse.maketru.com) is a free online rainwater harvesting and tank sizing calculator.

sections.heading: 2. Data collected
paragraphs: When you use the calculator, technical parameters (latitude, longitude, area, uses) are sent to our server and Open-Meteo to fetch rainfall. This data is not used to identify you personally.

sections.heading: 3. Cookies
paragraphs: WaterPulse may use browser local storage to remember your language choice. You can clear this data in your browser settings.
